sections.h2: Where is Lynn, Massachusetts, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Lynn is a coastal city in Essex County, about 10 miles northeast of Boston. It sits on Massachusetts Bay and borders Nahant, Swampscott, Salem, Peabody, Lynnfield, Saugus and Revere.

The Census Bureau lists about 13.5 square miles, and nearly a fifth of that is water. Nahant splits the shoreline in two, with Lynn Harbor to the south and Nahant Bay to the north. The only land link to Revere is the General Edwards Bridge over the Pines River, which matters if you are weighing a commute or a showing schedule.

More than a quarter of the city is Lynn Woods Reservation, which fills much of the northwest. Two beaches, Lynn Beach and King's Beach, face Nahant Bay.

Lynn is divided into Central, West Lynn and East Lynn, and each of those breaks into smaller areas that buyers and sellers tend to name by square or park.

  • Central: the downtown business district and Central Square.
  • West Lynn: Pine Hill, McDonough Square and Barry Park, Tower Hill and Austin Square along the Saugus River, The Commons, The Brickyard, Walnut Street and Lynnhurst, and Veteran's Village.
  • East Lynn: the Diamond District and Lynn Shore, Wyoma Square, The Highlands, The Fay Estates, Ward 1 along Lynnfield Street, Goldfish Pond, and The Meadow with Keaney Park.

A house near the water in the Diamond District sits in a different setting than a triple-decker near Central Square, and a cash buyer prices the two differently. When you describe your property, give the street and the nearest square.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Lynn's housing and economy?
sections.html:
Lynn was settled by Europeans in 1629 and made shoes from the 1600s until the last factory closed in 1981. At the start of the 20th century, 234 factories there produced more than a million pairs a day.

Electrical manufacturing followed. Thomson-Houston Electric, backed by Lynn shoe manufacturers, merged with Edison Electric in 1892 to form General Electric, and the jet engine plant has stayed in the city ever since.

Fire reshaped downtown twice. An 1889 blaze destroyed 296 buildings, including 142 homes. In 1981, a fire at former shoe factories on Broad and Washington Streets burned 17 downtown buildings. North Shore Community College's Lynn campus now occupies much of that burned area.

Mid-1800s estates and beach cottages lined the shoreline, and Lynn Shore Drive opened in 1910 and drew more building along the coast. Many of those structures sit in the National Register Diamond Historic District. Age is the thing to keep in mind: a Lynn house built over a century ago may carry old wiring, plaster and original systems, and that is when buyers who purchase as-is are most useful.

Other manufacturers have stayed too, including a polymer producer, a meat packer and the maker of Marshmallow Fluff. For a seller, steady local employment means a steady pool of people who need housing close to Lynn, though a cash sale does not depend on that.

sections.h2: How do the weather and the coast affect a Lynn house?
sections.html:
Lynn has cold, snowy winters and warm, humid summers, much like Boston. Climate normals for 1991 to 2020 show a January average high of 36.7 degrees and an average low of 20.8, with about 47.8 inches of precipitation across the year.

Those numbers describe long freeze and thaw seasons next to salt air. Roofs, gutters, chimneys, exterior paint and basement walls work harder in a place like that, and deferred upkeep shows up fast. A cash buyer who accepts a house as-is takes on that repair list, so you do not have to pay for it before the sale.

sections.h2: How do you get around Lynn, and what does transit mean for a sale?
sections.html:
Lynn has no interstate highway. Route 1A, Route 107, Route 129 and Route 129A run through the city, and the nearest interstate is the combined I-95 and Route 128 in Lynnfield.

  • Lynn station on the MBTA Commuter Rail Newburyport/Rockport Line, with about 20 minute service to North Station.
  • MBTA ferry route F5 from Blossom Street Pier to downtown Boston.
  • Numerous MBTA bus routes to Boston and neighboring communities.
  • Boston Logan International Airport, about 5 miles south.

A Blue Line extension to downtown Lynn has been proposed but not funded. Newer apartment buildings are going up within a half mile of Lynn station, including a 259 unit building on Monroe Street and a 331 unit waterfront project on Carroll Parkway, so the blocks near the station are changing. Homes farther out, such as near Lynn Woods, rely more on cars.

sections.h2: What do you need to know before selling a house in Lynn, MA?
sections.html:
The first step is a smoke and carbon monoxide alarm certificate: the Massachusetts Department of Fire Services states that you need a certificate of compliance from the local fire department when you sell or transfer a home.

Call the Lynn fire department as soon as you have a closing date. The department charges a fee, so ask what it is. Battery-powered smoke alarms older than 10 years must be replaced with alarms that have 10 year sealed batteries, are photoelectric and have a hush feature.

The state also taxes the deed itself. Under Chapter 64D, Section 1, the excise is two dollars for each five hundred dollars of consideration, or fraction of it, outside Barnstable County. On a sale price of $500,000 that works out to $2,000.

Massachusetts has two title systems, recorded land and registered land, and about 80 to 90 percent of properties are recorded land. The Mass.gov law library notes that real estate attorneys are a regular part of buying and selling, both by law and practice. Ask the city of Lynn, and your attorney, about any local permits tied to your house.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Lynn house work?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Lynn skips the buyer's mortgage, so there is no lender appraisal or loan approval to wait on. You still sign a purchase and sale agreement, clear title and close with a deed.

  1. You share the address, condition and your timeline.
  2. The buyer reviews the property and presents an offer.
  3. If you accept, an attorney handles the title work and the paperwork.
  4. The fire department certificate gets arranged according to what the contract says.
  5. You close at the registry date you agreed on and receive the proceeds.

Compare that with listing: showings, repairs a buyer's inspector requests, and financing that can fall through. Cash does not suit every seller, and an offer may land below a retail listing price. Weigh that against carrying costs and time.

faqs.q: Is Lynn a good place to sell a house quickly?
faqs.a: Lynn has a large, dense market, with 101,253 residents at the 2020 census and rail, ferry and bus service to Boston. How quickly a particular house sells depends on its condition, price and location. A cash offer can shorten the timeline because no mortgage approval is involved.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke detector certificate to sell in Lynn?
faqs.a: Yes. The Massachusetts Department of Fire Services says a certificate of compliance from the local fire department is required when you sell or transfer a home. Call the Lynn fire department for the fee and to schedule the inspection.

faqs.q: What is the Massachusetts deed excise tax?
faqs.a: It is two dollars for each five hundred dollars of consideration or fraction of it, set by Chapter 64D, Section 1, with a lower rate in Barnstable County. On a $400,000 sale, the tax is $1,600. Ask your attorney who pays it under your contract.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lynn house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer who purchases as-is accepts the house in its current condition, including repairs. You may still need the alarm certificate, and the contract should say who arranges it.

faqs.q: What if I inherited a house in Lynn?
faqs.a: You may need probate steps before you can sell, depending on how the property was held. Speak with a Massachusetts attorney or the probate court about authority to sell, then contact us about the house.
